analysis.overview: This course develops the financial mathematics required for the analysis of financial and insurance transactions, covering the mathematics of compound interest, analysis and valuation of annuities, bonds, loans and derivative securities, yield curves and immunisation, and an introduction to stochastic interest rate models and actuarial applications.

topics.title: Time Value of Money and Valuation of Cash Flows
subtopics: Present value and valuation of cash flows
Valuing contingent cash flows under different interest assumptions
learning_outcomes: Identify and clarify the concept of time value of money and its applications
Explain various types of interest and their applications
Articulate the relationship between present value, cash flows, and interest rate risk
topics.source_evidence: Module 1: Time Value of Money and Valuation of Cash Flows

topics.title: Loan Valuation and Project Appraisal Techniques
subtopics: Tax and transaction costs in valuation problems
learning_outcomes: Modify simple valuation problems to include tax and transaction costs
Apply financial valuation concepts to practical situations like investment appraisals
topics.source_evidence: Module 2: Loan Valuation and Project Appraisal Techniques

topics.title: Interest Rate Risk
subtopics: Relationship between interest rates and present value
learning_outcomes: Articulate the relationship between present value, cash flows, and interest rate risk
Assess the reasonableness of financial calculations and their underlying assumptions

topics.title: Valuation of Financial Securities
subtopics: Market conventions in securities and money markets
learning_outcomes: Describe and value various financial securities including bonds, shares, loans and annuities
Outline basic market conventions in securities and money markets
topics.source_evidence: analysis and valuation of annuities, bonds, loans and derivative securities

topics.title: Derivatives
learning_outcomes: Describe and value forwards, futures contracts and options

topics.title: Stochastic Returns
subtopics: Introduction to stochastic interest rate models
Expected value and variance of accumulation under stochastic interest
learning_outcomes: Develop formulas for the expected value and variance of accumulation under stochastic interest

assessments.name: Final Examination
assessments.date: Scheduled during the university exam period

study_notes: To pass the course, students must achieve a composite mark of at least 50 out of 100 and are required to attempt all assessment requirements.
The final examination is a 2-hour closed book, invigilated exam.
The assignment is an individual Excel-based task with at least 2 weeks to complete, submitted via Moodle; a Short Extension (3 days) is available.
Submitted work must be the student's own: mathematical solutions and any code must be written by the student without reference to another student's work.
Late submission penalty is 5% per day or part thereof (including weekends); assessments are not accepted after 5 days (120 hours) past the original deadline unless special consideration is approved.
Required textbooks: Broverman, Mathematics of Investment and Credit (8th Edition) and Sherris, Money and Capital Markets, Pricing, Yields and Analysis (2nd Edition).
Students are strongly encouraged to attend all classes and review lecture recordings.
Students should check the course Moodle website regularly (at least once every two days) for announcements.
Formative assessment details (forum discussions or online quizzes) will be announced at the start of the term.
Generative AI use: Not Applicable for the Final Examination; Simple Editing Assistance only for the Assignment and Formative Assessment (no text generation or paraphrasing).
Students may not circulate or post online any course materials without written permission from their instructor.
